question: What is the highest oxygen level at which any solid material was burned in PSI, and in which investigation?
claim: Among the PSI tests in the database with phase 'solid', the highest oxygen level is 22.2 % O2, in PSI-25 (BASS-II), where 14 of its 129 tests with an O2 value reached it.
summary_student: We checked every PSI test in the database with phase 'solid' that records an oxygen level, 140 tests in all. The highest oxygen level is 22.2 % O2, in the BASS-II investigation (PSI-25), where 14 of its 129 tests used it, with fuels named in the table as PMMA film, clear rod and 'Nomex natural (nomex III)'. All of these tests were run in microgravity.
summary_professional: Over the PSI tests in the database with phase 'solid' and a non-empty o2_pct_max (n = 140), the highest value is 22.2 % O2 in PSI-25 (BASS-II, column 'Calibrated initial O2 % by vol'), reached by 14 of its 129 tests. The next highest are 22.1 % O2 in PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II, 9 tests, values marked approximate and derived from measured CO2 production) and 21.7 % O2 in PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I, 2 tests). All counted rows have gravity 'microgravity', and none of these tables gives a pressure.

params.sql: SELECT lower(replace(investigation, '-', '')) || '_solid_o2_max' AS name, max(o2_pct_max) AS value, '% O2' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE phase = 'solid' AND scope = 'psi' AND o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT lower(replace(investigation, '-', '')) || '_solid_tests_with_o2' AS name, count(*) AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE phase = 'solid' AND scope = 'psi' AND o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT lower(replace(investigation, '-', '')) || '_solid_tests_at_highest_o2' AS name, count(*) AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE phase = 'solid' AND scope = 'psi' AND o2_pct_max = (SELECT max(o2_pct_max) FROM tests WHERE phase = 'solid' AND scope = 'psi') GROUP BY investigation, source_table

method.formula: The values returned by the SQL query in params, one row per value, each with the source rows it used.

assumptions: Every row with phase 'solid' is counted as a test in which the fuel was burned; the outcome column was not used to check ignition or extinction.

The oxygen level of a row is its o2_pct_max; for PSI-25 (BASS-II) it is read from the column 'Calibrated initial O2 % by vol', and for PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) and PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I) from their Percent O2 columns.
Volume percent and mole percent of O2 are treated as equal, as in the data catalog.
limitations: Covers only the PSI tests in the database with phase 'solid' and an O2 value, which are in PSI-25 (BASS-II), PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) and PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I); the tests with phase 'solid' in PSI-26 (BASS) and PSI-100 (SAFFIRE-III) give no O2 value and are not counted.
All counted rows have gravity 'microgravity'; this finding says nothing about burning at Earth gravity, and PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data for lunar or Mars gravity.
None of these tables gives a pressure, so the finding does not show the pressure at which these tests ran.
The PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) O2 values are marked approximate in the problems column and were derived from measured CO2 production, according to a note in its table.

The highest tested O2 level is not a flammability limit: it does not show whether these fuels would burn, or how fast, at higher oxygen levels, such as the lunar base atmosphere in the project's environment table.

chart.idea: Bar chart of the highest O2 level (% O2) of the tests with phase 'solid' in PSI-25 (BASS-II), PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) and PSI-98 (SAFFIRE-I), labeled with the number of tests behind each bar.
